sanskrit_shloka: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यद्वसूनां प्रातः सवनꣳ रुद्राणां माध्यन्दिनꣳ सवनमादित्यानां च विश्वेषां च देवानां तृतीयसवनम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
brahmavādino vadanti |
               yad vasūnāṃ prātaḥsavanam |
               rudrāṇāṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam |
               ādityānāṃ ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tṛtīyasavanam || ChUp_2,24.1 ||
translation: Before the commencement of the ‘Midday Extraction’, sitting behind the Agnīdhrīya Fire .— and facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Rudras .—

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Before the commencement of the ‘Midday Extraction’, sitting behind the Agnīdhrīya Fire .— and facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Rudras .—

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति, यत्प्रातःसवनं प्रसिद्धं तद्वसूनाम् । तैश्च प्रातःसवनसम्बद्धोऽयं लोको वशीकृतः प्रातःसवनेशानैः । तथा रुदॆर्माध्यन्दिनसवनेशानैः अन्तरिक्षलोकः । आदित्यैश्च विश्वैर्देवैश्च तृतीयसवनेशानैस्तृतीयो लोको वशीकृतः । इति यजमानस्य लोकोऽन्यः परिशिष्टो न विद्यते ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Similarly, sitting behind the Agnīdhṛīya Fire ,—i.e. the Dakṣiṇāgni ,—and facing the North , he sings the Sāma sacred to the Rudras , i.e. the Sāma of which the Rudras are the Deity,—for the purpose of attaining Vaiṛājya, (sovereignty of the Sky ).—(7-8)

sanskrit_shloka: क्व तर्हि यजमानस्य लोक इति स यस्तं न विद्यात्कथं कुर्यादथ विद्वान्कुर्यात् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
kva tarhi yajamānasya loka iti |
               sa yas taṃ na vidyāt kathaṃ kuryāt |
               atha vidvān kuryāt || ChUp_2,24.2 ||
translation: Where then is the Sacrificer’s Region? If one does not know this, how can he perform (the Sacrifice)? If he knows it, he should perform (it).—(2)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Where then is the Sacrificer’s Region? If one does not know this, how can he perform (the Sacrifice)? If he knows it, he should perform (it).—(2)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text:
अतः क्व तर्हि यजमानस्य लोकः, यदर्थं यजते ; न क्वचिल्लोकोऽस्तीत्यभिप्रायः — 
‘लोकाय वै यजते यो यजते’ ( ? )
 इति श्रुतेः । लोकाभावे च स यो यजमानः तं लोकस्वीकरणोपायं सामहोममन्त्रोत्थानलक्षणं न विद्यात् न विजानीयात् , सोऽज्ञः कथं कुर्यात् यज्ञम् , न कथञ्चन तस्य कर्तृत्वमुपपद्यत इत्यर्थः । सामादिविज्ञानस्तुतिपरत्वात् न अविदुषः कर्तृत्वं कर्ममात्रविदः प्रतिषिध्यते — स्तुतये च सामादिविज्ञानस्य, अविद्वत्कर्तृत्वप्रतिषेधाय च इति हि भिद्येत वाक्यम् । आद्ये च औषस्त्ये काण्डे अविदुषोऽपि कर्मास्तीति हेतुमवोचाम । अथ एतद्वक्ष्यमाणं सामाद्युपायं विद्वान्कुर्यात् ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: For the above reason, the question arises— When then is the Region for the Sacrificer ,—for attaining which, he performs the sacrifice? The sense of the question is that there is no Region for him.—In view of the Vedic Text—‘One who performs a sacrifice does so for the purpose of attaining a Region’,—if there is no Region for the Sacrificer, then if one who performs the sacrifice does not know the means of making the Region his own,—such means consisting in the knowledge of the ramifications of Sāma, Homa and Mantras ,—he is ignorant; and being ignorant, how could he perform a sacrifice? That is to say, in no way could he ever become a sacrificer ,— The purpose of all this is to eulogise the knowledge of Sāma and the sacrificial details, and it does not mean that the performance of the sacrifice is forbidden for one who knows merely the sacrificial ritual and is ignorant of the aforesaid Sāma and the rest. For if the sentence were taken as eulogising the knowledge of Sāma and the rest, and also as forbidding the performance by the ignorant,—then there would be a syntactical split. Further, in the section dealing with Uṣasti-Cākrāyaṇa we have already explained that the performance of sacrifices is permissible for the ignorant also.—On the other hand , if he knows the Sāma and other means, as are going to be described;—he should perform the sacrifice—(2)

sanskrit_shloka: पुरा प्रातरनुवाकस्योपाकरणाज्जघनेन गार्हपत्यस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य स वासवं सामाभिगायति ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
purā prātaranuvākasyopākaraṇāj jaghanena gārhapatyasyodāṅmukha upaviśya sa vāsavaṃ
            sāmābhigāyati || ChUp_2,24.3 ||
translation: Before the commencing of the ‘Morning Chant’, sitting behind the Gārhapatya Fire , and facing - the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Vasas.—(3)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Before the commencing of the ‘Morning Chant’, sitting behind the Gārhapatya Fire , and facing - the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to the Vasas.—(3)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: किं तद्वेद्यमिति, आह — पुरा पूर्वं प्रातरनुवाकस्य शस्त्रस्य प्रारम्भात् जघनेन गार्हपत्यस्य पश्चात् उदङ्मुखः सन् उपविश्य सः वासवं वसुदैवत्यं साम अभिगायति ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: The text proceeds to expound what it is that should be known by the Sacrificer;— Before —prior to—the commencing —beginning—of the ‘ morning chant’, sitting behind —at the back of— the Gārhapatya Fire ,—and facing the North —he sings the Sāma sacred to the Vasus ,—i.e. that of which the Vasas are the presiding deity .—(3)

sanskrit_shloka: लो३कद्वारमपावा३र्णू ३३ पश्येम त्वा वयं रा ३३३३३ हु३म् आ ३३ ज्या ३ यो ३ आ ३२१११ इति ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
lo 3 kadvāram apāvā 3 rṇū 33 |
               paśyema tvā vayaṃ rā 33333 hu 3 m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti || ChUp_2,24.4 ||
translation: ‘Open the gate of the Region, so that we may look upon Thee, for the purpose of attaining kingdom’.—(4)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: ‘Open the gate of the Region, so that we may look upon Thee, for the purpose of attaining kingdom’.—(4)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: लोकद्वारम् अस्य पृथिवीलोकस्य प्राप्तये द्वारम् अपावृणु हे अग्ने तेन द्वारेण पश्येम त्वा त्वां राज्यायेति ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: O Fire, open the door of the Region of the Earth,—i.e. for attaining this Region:—through that Door, we may look upon Thee,— for this purpose of attaining kingdom .—(4)

sanskrit_shloka: अथ जुहोति नमोऽग्नये पृथिवीक्षिते लोकक्षिते लोकं मे यजमानाय विन्दैष वै यजमानस्य लोक एतास्मि ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
atha juhoti |
               namo 'gnaye pṛthivīkṣite lokakṣite |
               lokaṃ me yajamānāya vinda |
               eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
               etā asmi || ChUp_2,24.5 ||
translation: Then he pours the libation (saying)—‘Adoration to Agni , dwelling on the earth, dwelling in the Region. Secure the Region for me, the Sacrificer! That would be the Sacrificer’s region to which I would go.’—(5)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Then he pours the libation (saying)—‘Adoration to Agni , dwelling on the earth, dwelling in the Region. Secure the Region for me, the Sacrificer! That would be the Sacrificer’s region to which I would go.’—(5)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: अथ अनन्तरं जुहोति अनेन मन्त्रेण — नमोऽग्नये प्रह्वीभूताः तुभ्यं वयं पृथिवीक्षिते पृथिवीनिवासाय लोकक्षिते लोकनिवासाय, पृथिवीलोकनिवासायेत्यर्थः ; लोकं मे मह्यं यजमानाय विन्द लभस्व ; एष वै मम यजमानस्य लोकः एता गन्ता अस्मि ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Then , after the above,—he pours the libation (in the fire)—with this Mantra.—‘Adoration to Agni , we bow down to Thee—Thou who art dwelling on the Earth, and dwelling in the Region ,’—i.e, dwelling in the Earthly Region I Secure—obtain —for me, the Sacrificer—the Region ; that would be the Sacrificer’s Region to which I would go.—(5)

sanskrit_shloka: अत्र यजमानः परस्तादायुषः स्वाहापजहि परिघमित्युक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति तस्मै वसवः प्रातःसवनं सम्प्रयच्छन्ति ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
               apajahi parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati |
               tasmai vasavaḥ prātaḥsavanaṃ saṃprayacchanti || ChUp_2,24.6 ||
translation: Herein, the Sacrificer, after the lapse of his life-span, (says)—‘ Svāhā ! Remove the bolt’, and saying this he stands up, and the Vasus offer to him the ‘Morning Extraction’—(6)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Herein, the Sacrificer, after the lapse of his life-span, (says)—‘ Svāhā ! Remove the bolt’, and saying this he stands up, and the Vasus offer to him the ‘Morning Extraction’—(6)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: अत्र अस्मिंल्लोके यजमानः अहम् आयुषः परस्तात् ऊर्ध्वं मृतः सन् इत्यर्थः । स्वाहेति जुहोति । अपजहि अपनय परिघं लोकद्वारार्गलम् — इति एतं मन्त्रम् उक्त्वा उत्तिष्ठति । एवमेतैर्वसुभ्यः प्रातःसवनसम्बद्धो लोको निष्क्रीतः स्यात् । ततस्ते प्रातःसवनं वसवो यजमानाय सम्प्रयच्छन्ति ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Herein —in the said Region,— the Sacrificer , after the lapse of his life -span ,—i.e. on death,—pours the libation, saying ‘ Svāhā ! Remove—take out—the bolt —the bar to the entrance to the Region’;—having recited this Mantra , he stands up .—By all these means the Region connected with the ‘Morning Extraction’ becomes secured from the Vasus ; hence these offer the ‘Morning Extraction’ to the Sacrificer.—(6)

sanskrit_shloka: पुरा माध्यन्दिनस्य सवनस्योपाकरणाज्जघनेनाग्नीध्रीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य सरौद्रं सामाभिगायति ॥ ७ ॥

purā mādhyandinasya savanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāgnīdhrīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa raudraṃ
            sāmābhigāyati || ChUp_2,24.7 || lo 3 kadvāramapāvār 3 ṇū 33 |

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: ‘Open the door......... for sovereignty of the Sky......... (7-8)

sanskrit_shloka: लो३कद्वरमपावा३र्णू३३ पश्येम त्वा वयं वैरा३३३३३ हु३म् आ३३ज्या३यो३ आ३२१११इति ॥ ८ ॥

translation: ‘Open the door......... for sovereignty of the Sky......... (7-8)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: ‘Open the door......... for sovereignty of the Sky......... (7-8)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: तथा आग्नीध्रीयस्य दक्षिणाग्नेः जघनेन उदङ्मुख उपविश्य सः रौद्रं साम अभिगायति यजमानः रुद्रदैवत्यं वैराज्याय ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Similarly, sitting behind the Agnīdhṛīya Fire ,—i.e. the Dakṣiṇāgni ,—and facing the North , he sings the Sāma sacred to the Rudras , i.e. the Sāma of which the Rudras are the Deity,—for the purpose of attaining Vaiṛājya, (sovereignty of the Sky ).—(7-8)

transliteration:
atha juhoti |
               nāmo vāyave 'ntarikṣakṣite lokakṣite |
               lokaṃ me yajamānāya vinda |
               eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
               etāsmi || ChUp_2,24.9 || atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
               apajahi parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati |

translation: Then he pours the libation, (saying)—‘Adoration to Vāyu, dwelling in the Sky, dwelling in the Region! Secure the Region for me, the Sacrificer.—That would be the Sacrificer’s Region to which I would go!’—(9)

commentaries.text: अन्तरिक्षक्षित इत्यादि समानम् ॥

               lo3kadvāramapāvā3rṇū33 |
               paśyema tvā vayaṃ sāmrā 33333 hu3m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti || ChUp_2,24.13 ||
translation: Before the commencement of the Third Extraction, sitting behind the Āhavanīya Fire , ānd facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to Āditya and that sacred to the Viśvedevas .—(11)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Before the commencement of the Third Extraction, sitting behind the Āhavanīya Fire , ānd facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to Āditya and that sacred to the Viśvedevas .—(11)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: तथा आहवनीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य सः आदित्यदैवत्यम् आदित्यं वैश्वदेवं च साम अभिगायति क्रमेण स्वाराज्याय साम्राज्याय ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Similarly, sitting behind the Āhavanīya Fire facing the North, he sings the Sāma sacred to Āditya —i.e. the Sāma of which Āditya is the deity,—and also the Sāma sacred to the Viśvedevas ,—for the purpose, respectively, of acquiring ‘sovereignty over Heaven’ and ‘supreme sovereignty.—(11, 12, 13)

sanskrit_shloka: अथ जुहोति नम आदित्येभ्यश्च विश्वेभ्यश्च देवेभ्यो दिविक्षिद्भ्यो लोकक्षिद्भ्यो लोकं मे यजमानाय विन्दत ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
atha juhoti |
               nama ādityebhyaś ca viśvebhyaś ca devebhyo divikṣidbhyo lokakṣidbhyaḥ |
               lokaṃ me yajamānāya vindata || ChUp_2,24.14 || eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
               etāsmy atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
               apahata parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati || ChUp_2,24.15 ||
translation: Then he pours the libation, (saying)—‘Adoration to the Ādityas and to the Viśvedevas , dwelling in Heaven and dwelling in the Region! Secure the region for me, the Sacrificer’.—(14)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Then he pours the libation, (saying)—‘Adoration to the Ādityas and to the Viśvedevas , dwelling in Heaven and dwelling in the Region! Secure the region for me, the Sacrificer’.—(14)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Dwelling in Heaven etc., etc.;—the rest is as before; the only difference is that the forms ‘ bindata ’ and ‘ apahata ’ are in the plural number (on account of the deities addressed being many in number).—All this is to be said by the Sacrificer, as is clearly indicated by the expressions ‘ etāsmi ’, (‘I would go’) and ‘ Atra Yajamānaḥ ’ (‘Herein the Sacrificer’).—(14, 15)

sanskrit_shloka: एष वै यजमानस्य लोक एतास्म्यत्र यजमानः परस्तादायुषः स्वाहापहत परिघमित्युक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
atha juhoti |
               nama ādityebhyaś ca viśvebhyaś ca devebhyo divikṣidbhyo lokakṣidbhyaḥ |
               lokaṃ me yajamānāya vindata || ChUp_2,24.14 || eṣa vai yajamānasya lokaḥ |
               etāsmy atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā |
               apahata parigham ity uktvottiṣṭhati || ChUp_2,24.15 ||
translation: Then he pours the libation, (saying)—‘Adoration to the Ādityas and to the Viśvedevas , dwelling in Heaven and dwelling in the Region! Secure the region for me, the Sacrificer’.—(14)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Then he pours the libation, (saying)—‘Adoration to the Ādityas and to the Viśvedevas , dwelling in Heaven and dwelling in the Region! Secure the region for me, the Sacrificer’.—(14)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: दिविक्षिद्भ्य इत्येवमादि समानमन्यत् । विन्दत अपहत इति बहुवचनमात्रं विशेषः । याजमानं त्वेतत् , एतास्म्यत्र यजमान इत्यादिलिङ्गात् ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Dwelling in Heaven etc., etc.;—the rest is as before; the only difference is that the forms ‘ bindata ’ and ‘ apahata ’ are in the plural number (on account of the deities addressed being many in number).—All this is to be said by the Sacrificer, as is clearly indicated by the expressions ‘ etāsmi ’, (‘I would go’) and ‘ Atra Yajamānaḥ ’ (‘Herein the Sacrificer’).—(14, 15)

sanskrit_shloka: तस्मा आदित्याश्च विश्वे च देवास्तृतीयसवनं सम्प्रयज्छन्त्येष ह वै यज्ञस्य मात्रां वेद य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
tasmā ādityāś ca viśve ca devās tṛtīyasavanaṃ saṃprayacchanti |
               eṣa ha vai yajñasya mātrāṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || ChUp_2,24.16 ||
translation: The Ādityas and the Viśvedevas offer to him the ‘Third Extraction’.—He, verily, knows the measure of the Sacrifice who knows this,—yea, who knows this.—(16)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: The Ādityas and the Viśvedevas offer to him the ‘Third Extraction’.—He, verily, knows the measure of the Sacrifice who knows this,—yea, who knows this.—(16)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: एष ह वै यजमानः एवंवित् यथोक्तस्य सामादेर्विद्वान् यज्ञस्य मात्रां यज्ञयाथात्म्यं वेद यथोक्तम् । य एवं वेदेति द्विरुक्तिरध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्था ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text:
He i.e. the Sacrificer who knows the Sāma and the details as described above, knows the measure —the real nature — of the Sacrifice , as described; Who knows this, yea, who knows this ’—the repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse.
End of the Section (24) of Discourse II
